name: How do contractors improve sound isolation in existing finished walls?
description: Contractors either add damped drywall layers over existing walls or open the wall to install acoustic batts, resilient channels, and airtight acoustic sealant.

mainEntity.name: How do contractors improve sound isolation in existing finished walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upgrading an existing wall usually involves adding dense layers, damping compounds, or isolated drywall assemblies. In retrofit projects, the least disruptive method is installing a layer of acoustic drywall or standard 5/8-inch gypsum over the existing surface using viscoelastic damping compound. When superior isolation is required, contractors remove the existing drywall down to the studs. This allows the installation of sound-attenuation mineral wool batts inside the cavity, along with resilient sound isolation clips and metal furring channels that decouple the new drywall from the framing. A key preparation step is identifying whether noise is traveling directly through the partition or flanking through HVAC ducts, door undercuts, and shared electrical boxes.
